"Let your light shine" Matthew 5:16
Welcome to Sissinghurst
We are a flourishing Church of England school set at the heart of a beautiful Kent village. As you arrive at our school, we hope that you will feel the sense of community and joyfulness which is created by our wonderful staff team and fantastic children.
We are blessed with a vibrant school community including passionate staff, children who are eager to learn, supportive parents and FOSS (Friends of Sissinghurst School). We aim to ensure every child is valued and cherished and that they have enjoyed many wonderful experiences to prepare them for the next stage in their education by the time they leave us.
We welcomed OFSTED in April 2025. They judged each area of our school to be good or outstanding. Read the full report here...
We had our SIAMS inspection in June 2026 which highlighted how successful our school is in enabling pupils and adults to flourish. Click here to read the report.
We are a growing school and have places currently in Y2 and Y6 (Sept 2026). Call the office or use the contact us button above if you would like your child to join us or to book a tour to see what we can offer your child.
Follow us on X @sissinghurstVA or Instagram @sissinghurstprimary (Click on 'Follow us' link also below)
Latest News
Continuing this week to revisit our rules and expectations. Many classes have developed and agreement or charter and signed up to this. An example here from Eagles Class
Leopards PSHE - learning all about dental care and why this is so important to be healthy. @kapow_primary
Elephants - Making predictions based on the bear's decision. Using what we know about the text and characters to help us.
Rhinos using a number line to help adding and counting.
We love animals and we definitely love Creepy Claws! We cannot wait for the club to start again Today we met Iris the pigmy hedgehog, Harry the Python from Africa and found out that Giant African millipedes grow up to 40 cm!! #curious #fun #engaging #welovefacts
Y5 RE lesson today where the children were discussing what qualities they think God should have and why. Great discussion and reflection.
Rhinos talking about how lives have changed for children over the years. Also setting expectations about how we present our learning - using a pencil and ruler here for our diagram.
Still loving our amazing sandpit #digging #playingtogether #tunnels
Everyone is reading after lunch in Eagles
Lions learning how to play and tidy up Opal style in the ballcourt this week
Dens and finding equipment to enhance our play make lunchtimes such fun. No arrows but who needs them with bows!
Lunchtime fun with new and old equipment. Umbrellas are the most popular today!
Deep discussion and thinking about creation in Y6 today
Practising handwriting for our early morning work. Making sure all letters are the correct height and formation.
Seeing like an artist. Drawing simple shapes then looking at adding shading and details. Well done Zebras! @kapow_primary

Religious Education
As a Church School, Religious Education has a high profile within our school curriculum. Our aim is to enable our children to become religiously literate and to help prepare them for life in the 21st Century. We follow the Kent Agreed Syllabus, with children in Key Stage One receiving one hour of RE teaching per week, rising to one and a quarter hours in Key Stage Two. Children learn significant theological concepts in Christianity as well as other world religions of Judaism, Islam, Sikhism and Hinduism. RE at Sissinghurst helps children with their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development as well as their own religious beliefs.
All RE lessons are enquiry based and each unit of lessons begins with a question. Children have the opportunity to reflect upon these questions through different learning styles such as art, stories, interactive games, studying artefacts, drama, music and visits. Pupils’ comments may be recorded in thought bubbles, pictures or on post-it notes and added to the classroom working wall.
Parents have the right to withdraw their child from all or part of RE lessons. This right of withdrawal exists for all pupils in all types of school, including schools with and without a religious designation. Students aged 18 or over have the right to withdraw themselves from RE. Parents also have the right to withdraw their child from part of RE and can do so without giving any explanation. We do ask if parents wish to withdraw their child from RE at Sissinghust, they do so in writing, for the attention of the Headteacher.

Christian Vision, Ethos & Values
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions any parent has to undertake.
At Sissinghurst Church of England Primary School in partnership with the Church, parents, and wider community, we offer an inclusive learning environment to nurture potential that enables all to be successful. Vibrant, rich curricular opportunities equip everyone with knowledge and skills to question, discuss and challenge.
Everyone’s talents are discovered and celebrated. We foster spiritual growth and reflection to find wonder and joy in the World together. As light bearers, our shared responsibility is to encourage each other to be compassionate and kind so we can all shine with integrity, humility and wisdom. We find courage to act when we know there is darkness, illuminating the World with God’s light and hope.
The school offers a wide range of experiences based on a knowledge-rich and sequential curriculum. We are proud of the range of clubs that we offer including wrap around care from 7:45am until 6pm.
We hope you will find the information on our website helpful. However, it is impossible to convey the friendly, caring atmosphere of the school or the commitment and enthusiasm of the staff. The only way is to see for yourself. Do not hesitate to make an appointment to look around the school via our contact form or call the office. You will be very welcome.
Our Christian Vision and Values
As a church school our vision is evident in all we offer. Click here to see a little more about our Christian distinctiveness. Our vision is underpinned by the Bible verses Matthew 5: 14-16. Jesus said … “You are the light of the world! A city can’t be hidden if it’s on top of a hill. People don’t light a lamp and put it under a bucket; they put it on a lampstand. Then it gives light to everybody in the house. That’s how you must shine your light in front of people! Then they will see what wonderful things you do, and they’ll give glory to your father in heaven... If I make you light-bearers, you don’t think I’m going to hide you under a bucket, do you? I’m putting you on a light stand. Now that I’ve put you there on a hilltop, on a light stand—shine! Keep open house; be generous with your lives."
We have 4 values - courage, forgiveness, service and kindness and each of these is evident in all aspects of school life. We constantly refer to our Christian values in our daily acts of collective worship and use them to promote a resilient attitude to learning and to celebrate and reflect on our expectations of behaviour. Different aspects of our Christian Values are reinforced and taught through many themes in collective worship, in RE and PSHE lessons and regular links are made with British values across the curriculum.
We celebrate children showing the school values using house points and certificate nominations in our Family Worship on Fridays.
Through reflection, learning and participation in school life, staff and pupils recognise that our school is not just a building, but a place where we become role-models, striving to live by the values we are promoting.
We persevere and are ready to learn, to try our best to make a difference to ourselves and others being strong and courageous. Joshua 1:9 "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go."
We treat everyone with respect and are ready to say sorry when we upset others. Ephesians 4:32 "Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other just as Christ God forgave you."
We look outwards at the world and at others to see how we can keep each other safe and help our community and our world. Acts 20:35 "It is more blessed to give than to receive."
We are ready to be kind, trustworthy friends like Jesus was to His disciples. With warm hearts we show love to others to help keep each other safe, ensuring we respect and celebrate everyone's uniqueness. Ephesians 4:32 "Be kind to one another."
Our School Prayer
Father, we ask that you would Bless us in our school Give us the strength to learn To be kind, to be fair And to look after others We are thankful for all your gifts

Curriculum and Class information
As a church school our vision is evident in all we offer. Our vision is underpinned by the bible verses Matthew 5: 14-16 where Jesus said “You are the light of the world! A city can’t be hidden if it’s on top of a hill. People don’t light a lamp and put it under a bucket; they put it on a lampstand. Then it gives light to everybody in the house. That’s how you must shine your light in front of people! Then they will see what wonderful things you do, and they’ll give glory to your father in heaven. If I make you light-bearers, you don’t think I’m going to hide you under a bucket, do you? I’m putting you on a light stand. Now that I’ve put you there on a hilltop, on a light stand—shine! Keep open house; be generous with your lives."
At Sissinghurst our curriculum has been designed with this vision and our school community in mind. It is what we believe our children need to flourish, thrive and be successful. Our offer challenges all our school community to be citizens who make a difference to each other, to the wider community and beyond.
Intent – ‘What’
We provide pupils with a knowledge-based curriculum that develops essential skills, equipping them for the next stage in their education and lives. Our curriculum is intended to ensure pupils develop a deep body of knowledge across subjects. We believe that through a well-sequenced, progressive curriculum, our children can develop the knowledge and skills to excel in a rapidly changing world. Our curriculum offer aims to address social disadvantage and close gaps. The curriculum is successfully adapted to meet the needs of pupils with SEND so they can develop their skills and knowledge to increase independence and gain the cultural capital they need to be successful. Our curriculum enables pupils to think critically about local and world issues and to interact successfully with the world around them. The way our curriculum content is selected allows vital concepts to be taught progressively throughout the school, allowing links to be made between different concepts and vital learning to be rehearsed and retrieved when needed in order to build ‘cumulative fluency’ across all subjects. Our curriculum is not only well-sequenced, but it is ambitious and ensures we have high expectations for all children in our school. We understand the importance of quality across all subject areas because every subject plays a part in a child’s holistic growth and knowledge development. We place importance on reading and reading across the curriculum as it is crucial to learning. We prioritise this from the moment children start in EYFS. Through the promotion of British and school values we ensure that our curriculum focuses on the development of the whole child and values all aspects of what makes our children unique and special.
Implementation – ‘How’
Our knowledge-rich approach is delivered by teachers with strong pedagogical knowledge. There is a focus on teachers developing highly effective learning sequences. Throughout the teaching of these highly effective learning sequences we ensure that retrieval activities are utilised and feedback from this used to inform the rest of the learning sequences. Class teachers are empowered to enact the curriculum in their classrooms using the resources provided for them in different subject areas. The focus on children ‘knowing and remembering more’ means we have worked to ensure that teaching sequences build in opportunities for retrieval and rehearsal of core concepts to ensure these transfer into long-term memory. A teaching backwards approach in classrooms focuses on what is essential knowledge at the end of a teaching sequence and this is used to ensure that sequences are well planned towards children acquiring this knowledge. Scaffolds and supports are used to ensure that all children have the opportunity to reach the high expectations of the curriculum. In addition to this, by focusing on slowing learning down we try to ensure that our focus remains on depth and allows knowledge to be retained and remembered whilst still ensuring there is challenge present in all learning sequences. There is strength in the school in following the ‘I do, we do, you do’ model which ensures that all aspects of learning are modelled clearly by the class teacher, time is then given in groups to practise and reinforce learning before children are given the chance to work independently. This approach allows teachers to quickly check pupils’ understanding and correct any misunderstandings during the ‘we do’ stage. Our dedication to reading is seen in classrooms with it being prioritised across the curriculum and ensuring we have a rigorous and sequential approach to the teaching of phonics and spelling. To ensure quality across all areas of the curriculum, we employ a specialist music teacher to teach the trumpet in Y3. In order to support teachers to deliver a highly effective knowledge-rich curriculum we use carefully selected schemes when appropriate. Finally, pupils’ engagement with the curriculum is monitored effectively and communicated with parents and other colleagues if there are any concerns.
In order to support our class teachers in the implementation phase we have a robust approach to professional development that tackles two strands. Firstly, ‘content knowledge’ which focuses on ensuring teachers have the required subject knowledge to deliver the curriculum. This support is achieved by giving additional planning time, ensuring expert subject leaders are available to support teachers and through high-quality professional development. Secondly, ‘pedagogical content knowledge’ which focuses on ensuring teachers have the required knowledge of good teaching to enact the curriculum in the classroom.
Impact – ‘How Well’
The impact of our curriculum is where we focus on and measure the quality of outcomes. Essentially we are focused upon ensuring that pupils are making progress in what they need to know and remember. Teachers and leaders check that they are learning what is intended in the curriculum. This measuring is completed in a variety of ways and all ongoing assessment and monitoring is vital. What we see in classrooms and what we hear when we speak to children are the drivers for assessing our intent and adapting and improving our implementation. Class teachers are responsible for the ongoing assessment of their children. This is completed through mini-plenaries and carefully planned questioning. These are both vital tools in allowing classroom teachers to see the impact of the curriculum they are delivering and adapt it accordingly to the needs of the children. Children are regularly spoken to by subject leaders and senior leaders to ensure they understand their lived experience of the curriculum with a particular focus on what they have learnt and remembered. Children will know what they are being asked to learn and, more importantly, why they are being asked to learn it, which allows them to make meaningful links between their current and previous learning. They will become increasingly confident when discussing and critiquing their learning. Regular feedback, both written and verbal, between the teacher and learner helps this learning journey to be tracked and monitored. There are clear expectations for each year group and subject, so teachers and learners know what has been achieved and the next learning steps. These are also used at the end of the year to make judgements about whether children are working at the expected standard or not. Summative assessments (Y2 to Y6) are used in autumn and summer terms and help to inform planning and judgement in core subjects (Maths and Literacy) and data from national tests (SATS). We work hard to ensure that we monitor the progress of our SEND and disadvantaged children and provide additional support whenever needed to ensure they acquire the knowledge and cultural capital needed for them to be successful.

If you would like to know more about our curriculum, please speak with any teacher or contact the Headteacher via the school office.

Extended Services and Clubs
We offer a wide range of school clubs throughout the day including before school, lunchtime and after school opportunities. We believe that all children should have the opportunity to experience a range of clubs including music, arts, sports and drama opportunities. Many of our school clubs are free, some of our school clubs need to be paid for however we encourage all children to take part in a club and make provision for families where the cost of clubs may be prohibitive.
As a parent of our school, if you have any skills or talents and would like to offer a club, we are always keen to offer more, please contact the office so we can make necessary arrangements for this. Children would love the following clubs if you can help : book club, art, sewing, knitting, lego, games, film, fitness.
Our Breakfast and After-School Clubs are open to any child who attends our school. The club runs Monday through Friday when the school is open to children (both do not run on INSET days and during school holidays). Breakfast Club from 7.45 am and After-School Club until 6pm.
We accept tax-free childcare vouchers and childcare grant payments. If parents are in receipt of these schemes please show evidence to the office and we can adapt Arbor so you can book childcare without paying up front. See document below for more information on this.
Drop-off for breakfast club is at 7.45am only. Pick-up for after-school club is by 6pm daily.
Can I book wraparound care on the day I need it?
Wraparound Care can be booked via Arbor, our school payment system.

Forest School
We are blessed to be set at the heart of a beautiful Kent Village, surrounded by nature. We believe the outdoors can be a great place for learning and therefore run forest sessions each week.
Forest School originated in Scandinavia in the 1950s and was intended as a way to teach children about the natural world and environmental issues. Throughout the year, all classes will spend afternoons having forest learning time with Mrs Walker. During these sessions children spend time regularly in our wild area learning through fun and exciting outdoor activities. They learn how to co-operate and work with others to solve problems, use their own initiative and manage risks.
We also are developing our pond area, reflection space and gardens that our Planet Defenders are very excited about. They are particularly proud to be demonstrating 'service' by growing our own vegetables.

If you wish to apply for a school place during the academic year, please complete the KCC In Year Application form and return to the office at office@sissinghurst.kent.sch.uk. Photos of the completed pages are accepted.
In Year Admission Form
Please email the school office on office@sissinghurst.kent.sch.uk if you wish to book onto a tour for any year group admission to Sissinghurst Primary School. The Headteacher is always happy to offer you a tour so you can make an informed decision.
We currently have spaces in Y2 and Y6 (Sept 2026). We have a waiting list for other year groups, but if you are interested in a place with us, whatever year group, we would love to hear from you.
We are offering a Headteacher talk and tours on the following dates :
Monday 2 November 9:30am and 1:45pm
Thursday 5th November 1:45pm
Please book your tour by completing the following form: Autumn School Tours Reception Class September 2027 – Fill in form
In deciding where you would like your child to go to school, it is really important to find out as much as you can about the schools themselves.
The local authority (LA) coordinates all admissions for children starting school for the first time and the link below will direct you to the Kent County Council website where you will find all the information that you require. If you have a child in any other year group, and would like to enquire about places, then please do so directly through the school office. https://www.kent.gov.uk/education-and-children/schools/school-places/primary-school-places#tab-3 You can make applications from 7 November 2026 for your place.
How to apply - Applications for children starting Reception in September 2027 open on Friday 6th November 2026 and close on Thursday 14 January 2027. If you provided an email address on your application Kent County Council will email you on Thursday 15 April 2027 after 4pm to tell you which school you have been offered. You can also log in from 5pm on Thursday 15 April 2027 to view your offer online. Offer emails will be sent to the email address provided on your application.
Appeals - If your child is due to start Primary school in September 2027, you can appeal if you are refused a place at one of your preferred schools on National Offer Day (15 April 2027). You need to submit your appeal in by Tuesday 18 May 2027 for it to be considered by July 2027, and can only appeal for schools that were named on your original application form. Any appeals received after this time will be heard within 40 school days from the deadline, or where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education.
For late applications, appeals should be heard within 40 school days from the deadline for lodging appeals where possible, or within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education.
If you wish to apply under our faith-based criteria you will need to complete an additional form called a Supplementary Information Form (SIF).
